key_insight: WildWorld supplies a large-scale dataset that decouples actions from raw pixels by pairing diverse, semantically meaningful action spaces with explicit underlying state annotations, enabling learning of action-conditioned latent dynamics rather than pixel-action shortcuts.
problem_solved: Existing video/world-model datasets rarely offer semantically rich, diverse action spaces or explicit state information, so models end up learning direct pixel-to-action correlations instead of true state-mediated dynamics. WildWorld fills this gap to support principled action-conditioned world modeling.
method: Assemble large-scale interactive sequences where each timestep contains (visual observation, explicit latent state, and semantically meaningful action) triplets.
Design the dataset so actions affect an underlying state representation rather than being tied only to visual changes, enabling models to learn state-driven transition dynamics.
Provide standardized splits and evaluation tasks to train and benchmark action-conditioned generative world models for downstream control and simulation.
impact: Researchers can train more robust, controllable generative world models that generalize across actions and states, improving simulation fidelity, planning, and RL performance—particularly for interactive domains like ARPGs.
visual_elements: State–Action–Observation pipeline diagram: arrows showing actions -> latent state -> rendered observations to illustrate decoupling.

Sample sequence frames with overlayed explicit state vectors and action labels to show triplet annotations.

paper_title: WildWorld: A Large-Scale Dataset for Dynamic World Modeling with Actions and Explicit State toward Generative ARPG
paper_authors: Zhen Li, Zian Meng, Shuwei Shi, Wenshuo Peng, Yuwei Wu
